mistakes: No plan levels or setups today (calendar only), so this review covers the user's Opening Range trades and price action, not OANDA fills.
Two trades had no stop loss (GBP/USD T1 and the second NZD/USD T2). That breaks the set-and-forget rule, even though GBP/USD finished well.
Four trades were closed by hand instead of at the stop or target (GBP/USD, both NZD/USD, USD/CHF T2).
Slippage: EUR/USD T1 filled 2.4 pips worse and USD/CAD T2 filled 6.6 pips worse than the signal. The USD/CAD loss grew to −1.69R because of it.
EUR/USD T1 stop was placed 3.7 pips from the signal's stop.
NZD/USD T2 was entered twice on the same signal, doubling the risk on one idea.
Closed losses add up to −3.28R. At 2% per R that is past the −4% daily loss limit; close times aren't in the block, so it can't be told whether any trade was opened after the limit was hit.
lessons: Repeat: Take the T1 signals at the signal price with the signal's stop and target. USD/CHF T1 (+1.83R) was textbook, and the EUR/USD T2 loss was a clean −1R as planned.
Improve tomorrow: Every trade gets the signal's stop before it is placed, one entry per signal, and no entries more than a pip or two away from the signal price. Skip a signal rather than chase it.

Most profit: T1 paid best. Six of seven T1 signals hit +2R (only USD/JPY stopped), and the T1 trades taken made +6.14R. The T2 trades closed so far lost −2.16R, and four T2 signals stopped out. Taking only T1 (adding the missed AUD/USD, USD/CAD and NZD/USD T1 targets, +2R each) and skipping T2 would have made far more.
